error_note: High ACTH is characteristic of familial glucocorticoid deficiency, but this is a 9th-specimen code after an unspecified (XXX) challenge, so 'high' has no defined meaning and is not a baseline ACTH.
cblE causes homocystinuria without methylmalonic acidemia; the disease record gives the phenotype as excluded (0%) and a positive association was emitted anyway.
The pre-CRH sample is effectively a baseline ACTH, but ACTH deficiency is only an occasional feature of this pituitary hormone deficiency and a low basal ACTH is a poor way to show it.
HMG-CoA synthase deficiency gives fasting hypoketotic hypoglycemia; a low glucose 1 hour after an IV glucose load is a different finding, and hypoglycemia is shared by over 200 diseases.
Hypomagnesemia has been reported in dopamine beta-hydroxylase deficiency but is not a characteristic or diagnostic finding, and the 'frequent' frequency looks overstated.
Hyperglycemia defines type 1 diabetes, but this is a lactose tolerance timepoint where a glucose rise is the normal response and 'high' has no diabetic criteria.
The disease annotation to 'Abnormal circulating enzyme concentration or activity' refers to porphobilinogen deaminase; lipase is not raised in acute intermittent porphyria.
Abnormal glucose homeostasis is a real feature of this syndrome, but a 10-hour sample after an unspecified challenge has no defined 'high', and hyperglycemia is nonspecific.
The test measures erythrocyte uroporphyrin, while the bridging phenotype and the finding in homozygous variegate porphyria is raised erythrocyte protoporphyrin.
Diabetes is common in atypical Werner syndrome, but glucose 1 minute after an IV glucose bolus is high in everyone and is not a hyperglycemia measurement.
The disease record lists raised lactate as excluded (0%) in hereditary spastic paraplegia 12, yet a positive association was emitted.
A low allergen-specific IgE to an animal dander mix is a normal finding and says nothing about the total immunoglobulin abnormalities (hypogammaglobulinemia, hyper-IgM) of NEMO deficiency.
Raised ACTH is obligate in familial glucocorticoid deficiency, but a 2-hour sample after an unspecified (XXX) challenge has no defined 'high' and is not a baseline ACTH.
A low fruit-mix specific IgE is the normal non-sensitised state and is not an abnormality of circulating immunoglobulin concentration.
Congenital myasthenic syndromes are genetic and seronegative; the record lists AChR antibody positivity as excluded (0%), so a positive association is the reverse of the truth.
Familial renal glucosuria is defined by glucosuria with normal blood glucose; the record marks hyperglycemia as explicitly not a feature.
An HIV-2 antibody is an antibody to a pathogen, not an autoantibody, and the disease record lists autoantibody positivity as excluded (0%) anyway.
The code is the ratio of blueberry-specific IgE to total IgE, not a specific IgE level; a high ratio can reflect a low total IgE rather than a raised specific IgE.
A negative Brussels sprout RAST class bears on one allergen and barely argues against raised IgE to plant foods as a class; the code is also deprecated in LOINC.
Hypernatremia is at most an occasional incidental finding in carbonic anhydrase VA deficiency, whose characteristic results are hyperammonemia, lactic acidosis and hypoglycemia.
CD34 marks hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells, not T cells, and the code is a fraction of cells rather than a count.
Suppressed C-peptide occurs only with the IGF-2 mediated hypoglycemia (Doege-Potter syndrome) seen in under 5% of solitary fibrous tumors, and is meaningful only during hypoglycemia.
A normal result on a five-tree pollen mix cannot rule out raised IgE to plant products in general, which covers every other pollen, food and plant allergen.
A normal chick pea result cannot rule out raised IgE to plant foods as a class, and the code is a specific-to-total IgE ratio rather than a level.

The record entry describes first-tier screening by propionylcarnitine (C3), not methylmalonate; dried blood spot methylmalonate is a genuine second-tier test, so the link is true but does not match the entry it was drawn from.

A TSH below 0.4 shows TSH suppression, not hyperthyroidism: it also occurs in subclinical disease, central hypothyroidism, nonthyroidal illness and early pregnancy, and needs free T4, as the curator text itself says.
tTG IgA is usually negative in collagenous sprue and serves to separate it from celiac disease; this pertinent negative is coded as a biomarker with expected result 'other'.

The band lies between the critical limits and spans both normal and clearly abnormal hematocrits, so the statement is true but only because critical limits were used as a band for a normal/abnormal phenotype.
An eGFR below 15 defines category G5, but end-stage renal failure requires chronicity; a single creatinine-based eGFR is equally low in acute kidney injury, where the equation is not valid.

The AT_TARGET bands are treatment target ranges for children on levothyroxine and extend above the reference interval (Cobas target up to 25.8 pmol/L), so an at-target value does not rule out an abnormal free T4.
